version_history.change: Required no critical structural alerts (PAINS + Brenk combined, absolute zero).

Changed structural-alert qualification to: No new Brenk structural alerts relative to the Ambroxol seed (plain set difference on alert-TYPE identifiers, A_new = A_i \ A_seed). PAINS split out as a separate, absolute gate (N_PAINS = 0).
version_history.reason: Fixture validation (synthetic data, not real GenMol/MolMIM output) demonstrated that the v1.0 rule structurally excluded Ambroxol itself and nearly all faithful on-scaffold analogues -- Ambroxol's free aromatic primary amine trips RDKit's Brenk 'aniline' alert -- making qualified yield degenerate (mostly measuring scaffold escape) rather than informative.
version_history.basis_for_that_claim: Derived from applying the alert catalogs to the seed molecule alone (frozen_date 2026-08-14 SMILES); no primary-run GenMol/MolMIM data existed when this amendment was made.

version_history.change: Replaced v1.1's plain type-level set difference with an INSTANCE-aware, atom-mapped rule: a candidate Brenk occurrence counts as seed-inherited only if it has the same alert type AND its matched atoms equal a seed alert instance's atoms mapped onto the candidate via an MCS atom correspondence. Gate renamed no_new_structural_alerts_relative_to_seed -> no_new_unmapped_structural_alert_instances.
version_history.reason: v1.1's type-only rule had a real, identified flaw: it could not distinguish 'the seed's own aniline' from 'an unrelated second aniline introduced elsewhere' -- both are just the type aniline under a plain set. A generator could freely proliferate or relocate an allowlisted alert type without penalty. The instance-aware rule requires positional correspondence to the seed's specific alert occurrence, not just type identity.
version_history.basis_for_that_claim: Identified and fixed by reasoning about the rule's definition and testing it on synthetic molecules (including benzidine, used only to probe RDKit's FilterCatalog matching behavior), not from any GenMol/MolMIM primary-run data.
version_history.implementation_note: While implementing this, found and worked around a real RDKit behavior: FilterCatalogEntry.GetFilterMatches(mol) returns only the FIRST occurrence of a pattern per entry, even when a molecule has multiple disjoint matches. See seed_alert_catalog.json:known_rdkit_limitation_worked_around.

PAINS.note: PAINS does not get seed-relative treatment (Section 5). If future fixture validation shows Ambroxol itself triggers a PAINS rule, that requires another explicitly versioned protocol amendment -- it is not implied by this one.

seed_relative_alert_rule.formal_definition: Let M_seed = {m_1, ..., m_k} be the seed's own Brenk alert INSTANCES, each m = (alert_type, atom_set_in_seed). For candidate i, M_i is its corresponding set of instances (alert_type, atom_set_in_candidate). Given a seed-to-candidate atom correspondence f (see instance_mapping below), a candidate instance m=(t,S) is seed_inherited iff there exists a seed instance (t, S_seed) in M_seed with every atom of S_seed covered by f and f(S_seed) == S exactly. M_new,i = {m in M_i : m is not seed_inherited}. Candidate passes the gate iff |M_new,i| = 0.
seed_relative_alert_rule.supersedes_v1.1_definition: v1.1 used a plain set difference on alert-TYPE identifiers only (A_new = A_i \ A_seed), which could not distinguish the seed's own alert instance from an unrelated second occurrence of the same type. v1.2 requires positional correspondence via f, not just type identity -- fixing that specific, identified flaw.
seed_relative_alert_rule.seed_inherent_allowlist_file_note: Canonical frozen record of M_seed, including each instance's matched atom indices, generated once from the seed alone. The evaluator recomputes M_seed at runtime from the frozen seed SMILES and hard-fails (does not silently proceed) if it disagrees with this file, per the 'no additional alert after inspecting results' policy.

instance_mapping.method: rdkit.Chem.rdFMCS.FindMCS([seed_mol, candidate_mol]) -> GetSubstructMatch on both mols using the same MCS query (uniquify=default first match) -> zip the two atom-index tuples to build f: seed_atom_idx -> candidate_atom_idx.
instance_mapping.correspondence_test: A seed instance's atom set S_seed is only usable if EVERY atom in S_seed has an entry in f (partial coverage disqualifies that seed instance for this candidate, fail-safe toward 'new'). A candidate occurrence is seed_inherited only if its own matched atom set equals f(S_seed) EXACTLY for some seed instance of the same alert type.
instance_mapping.known_simplification_not_resolved: GetSubstructMatch returns only the first match RDKit finds for the MCS query. For a seed or candidate with symmetry-equivalent substructures, a different, equally valid atom correspondence could exist and change the classification. Not resolved by trying all automorphisms in this version -- documented so it can be revisited if it causes a misclassification on real data, not silently assumed away.
instance_mapping.mcs_timeout_handling: If the MCS search times out, the best-so-far mapping is still used; affected molecules are logged (alert_mapping_timed_out) and printed as a warning by the evaluator.
instance_mapping.rdkit_matching_workaround: FilterCatalogEntry.GetFilterMatches(mol) only returns each pattern's FIRST occurrence, not all disjoint matches -- verified on benzidine. get_brenk_instances() works around this by extracting the underlying SMARTS query mol and calling mol.GetSubstructMatches(pattern, uniquify=True) directly. See seed_alert_catalog.json:known_rdkit_limitation_worked_around.

unique.description: First occurrence of this canonical SMILES within its own replicate (within-run dedup, not pooled across replicates)

not_exact_seed_copy.description: Not an exact Ambroxol copy (identity check on canonical SMILES, independent of the Tanimoto similarity band below)

pains.description: Zero PAINS_A/B/C catalog hits. Absolute, not seed-relative (Section 5).

no_new_unmapped_structural_alert_instanc.description: PRIMARY structural-alert gate (v1.2). No Brenk alert OCCURRENCE that fails to map, atom-for-atom, onto a corresponding seed alert instance (see seed_relative_alert_rule / instance_mapping). Seed-inherited instances (e.g. Ambroxol's own aniline at its own position) are allowed; a second, independent occurrence of the same alert type is not. All instances are always reported, never silently dropped.

notes: These are a predefined operational triage policy for comparing generators, not claims that molecules outside these thresholds cannot become drugs (DESCRIPTION.md Section 4).

Thresholds must not be changed after observing which tool wins (DESCRIPTION.md Section 15). See 'version_history' above for why the one exception (the structural-alert gate) does not violate that rule: it was derived from the seed alone, before any primary-run comparison existed.
Qualified candidate yield Y_chemical = N_pass_all_gates / N_requested, evaluated per replicate (denominator is requested_molecules_per_replicate, not N_valid).
'unique' is evaluated within a single replicate's output, matching the per-replicate Y_chemical denominator; pooled cross-replicate duplication is reported separately as a diagnostic, not as a gate.

Report three Brenk rates alongside Y_chemical (instance-level, v1.2): R_Brenk (fraction of valid molecules with ANY Brenk alert instance), R_seed_alert (fraction whose instances are ALL seed-inherited, none new), R_new_alert (fraction with >=1 new/unmapped instance). R_new_alert is the one used for qualification; the gap between R_Brenk and R_new_alert is itself evidence for this paper's central thesis.
Allowlisting a seed-inherited Brenk instance does not mean it is safe or biologically irrelevant -- it is a fixed, reported property of the starting chemotype, not a judgment about tolerability.

Not permitted: manually exempting alert instances molecule-by-molecule; adding new alert-instance exceptions to seed_alert_catalog.json after looking at benchmark winners; exempting a newly generated functional group merely because it appears frequently; removing structural-alert reporting from the analysis.
